official_tasks.task: Enforce multi-step workflow ordering and escalation handoffs with programmatic prerequisites rather than prompt wording, and compile structured handoff summaries for human agents.
Choose between fixed prompt chains and adaptive decomposition for a workflow, including per-file review passes plus a cross-file integration pass.
Write tool descriptions and boundaries (inputs, examples, edge cases, when-not-to-use) that disambiguate similar tools, and rename or split overlapping tools.
Organize CLAUDE.md across user, project and directory levels, modularize with imports and a rules directory, and diagnose why a teammate is not receiving instructions.
Run Claude Code in CI non-interactively with structured JSON output, project context via CLAUDE.md, independent review sessions, and de-duplication against prior findings.
Write explicit categorical review criteria with severity definitions instead of vague or confidence-based instructions to cut false positives and preserve developer trust.
Use a small set of targeted few-shot examples to stabilize format, show ambiguous-case reasoning, separate acceptable patterns from real issues, and reduce extraction hallucination.
Enforce schema-compliant output via tool use with JSON schemas, choose the right tool_choice mode, and design nullable fields and enum escape values to prevent fabrication.
Build validation-retry loops that feed specific errors back to the model, recognize when retries cannot help because data is missing, and add self-check fields such as calculated vs stated totals.
Select between synchronous and batch processing by latency tolerance, handle batch failures by correlation id, and size submission windows against an SLA.
Design multi-instance and multi-pass reviews: independent reviewer without generator reasoning, per-file passes plus integration pass, and confidence reporting for routing.
Select a Claude model by weighing capability, latency and cost tradeoffs.
Design system prompts, templates and guardrails.
Apply zero-shot, few-shot and chain-of-thought prompting appropriately.
Optimize context windows and token usage.
Reuse prompts via caching, modular prompts and Skills.
Diagnose system faults such as prompt failure, hallucination and model mismatch.
Write effective prompts for business and technical tasks.

Iterate on prompts to raise output quality.

Manage configuration: CLAUDE.md, settings.json, model version pinning, prompt versioning and plugin dependencies.

docs_facts.fact: GA. JSON outputs go in output_config.format with type json_schema; constrained decoding guarantees valid, schema-conformant output (strict tool use via strict: true is the sibling feature; both can be combined). Objects need additionalProperties: false. Unsupported: recursive schemas, numeric and string-length constraints, external $ref, minItems beyond 0/1. Refusals (stop_reason refusal) and max_tokens truncation can yield output that does not match. Incompatible with citations (400) and message prefilling. SDK helpers: client.messages.parse with output_format (Pydantic), zodOutputFormat() (Zod).
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: The old output_format parameter and beta header structured-outputs-2025-11-13 are deprecated; the parameter moved to output_config.format and no header is needed.

docs_facts.fact: Current lineup per the overview page: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1; demanding reasoning, long-horizon agentic work, $10/$50 per MTok), Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5; agentic coding and knowledge work, $4/$20), Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5; speed/intelligence balance, $2/$10), Claude Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5; high-volume low-latency, from $0.10/$0.50). All: 1M context, 128K max output, adaptive thinking, knowledge cutoff Jun 2026. Default effort: high (Fable, Sonnet) or medium (Opus 5.5, Haiku 5.5). Mythos models appear on other pages as limited-availability. Legacy still available: claude-fable-5, claude-opus-5, claude-opus-4-8, claude-opus-4-7, claude-opus-4-6, claude-opus-4-5-20251101, claude-sonnet-5, claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-haiku-4-5-20251001.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: A fourth top tier (Fable) and the 5.5 generation exist; exam items built around 4.x Opus/Sonnet/Haiku name legacy models. Dateless IDs from the 4.6 generation on are themselves pinned snapshots.

docs_facts.fact: Legacy but Active; ID claude-haiku-4-5-20251001. Earliest possible retirement on the Anthropic-operated platforms: not sooner than October 15, 2026 (no deprecation notice yet in the table). Recommended replacement target in older deprecations was this model; Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5) is the current Haiku. Minimum cacheable prompt 4,096 tokens.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: Retirement floor of Oct 15, 2026 is already passed as of 2026-10-28 while the table still shows Active; watch for a deprecation notice.

docs_facts.fact: Legacy but Active; ID claude-opus-4-8; not sooner than May 28, 2027. It is now the replacement target named for retired Opus 4 / 4.1 / Opus 3 in the deprecations history. 1,024-token minimum for caching; supports tool search and structured outputs.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: Newer Opus (5, 5.5) exist; questions treating Opus 4.8 as newest are stale.

docs_facts.fact: Lifecycle states: Active, Legacy, Deprecated, Retired. At least 60 days notice for publicly released models. Deprecated now: claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 (deprecated 2026-09-30, retires 2026-11-30, replacement claude-sonnet-5-5); claude-mythos-preview deprecated 2026-06-09. Retired: claude-opus-4-1-20250805 (2026-08-05), claude-opus-4-20250514 and claude-sonnet-4-20250514 (2026-06-15), claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219 and claude-3-5-haiku-20241022 (2026-02-19), claude-3-haiku-20240307 (2026-04-20). Parameter deprecation: temperature, top_p, top_k removed in API version 2026-10-21 (400 even at default). Bedrock and Google-managed set their own dates.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: Sonnet 4.5 retires 2026-11-30 (30 days from today); sampling-parameter removal landed 2026-10-21.

docs_facts.fact: Set via output_config.effort. Level names seen in the Claude Code docs: low, medium, high, xhigh, max (the effort page excerpt read here showed medium and max explicitly). Default is high on most models; Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 default to medium (per this page; the models overview shows Fable 5.1 and Sonnet 5.5 as high). Passing the model's default is identical to omitting it. max is available on the Fable/Mythos models and Opus 5.5/5/4.8 among others. Thinking is adaptive on current models; manual budget_tokens extended thinking is not accepted on later models.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: Extended thinking with budget_tokens is deprecated on Opus 4.6/Sonnet 4.6 and rejected on later models; effort plus adaptive thinking replaces it.
